closing.label: Śānti mantra

sanskrit.iast:
oṃ saha nāvavatu |
saha nau bhunaktu |
saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai |
tejasvi nāvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai ||
oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ ||
sanskrit.deva:
ॐ सह नाववतु ।
सह नौ भुनक्तु ।
सह वीर्यं करवावहै ।
तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॥
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥

lines.iast: oṃ saha nāvavatu
saha nau bhunaktu
saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai
tejasvi nāvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai
oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ

padaccheda.iast: oṃ saha nau avatu saha nau bhunaktu saha vīryam karavāvahai tejasvi nau adhītam astu mā vidviṣāvahai oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
padaccheda.deva: ॐ सह नौ अवतु सह नौ भुनक्तु सह वीर्यम् करवावहै तेजस्वि नौ अधीतम् अस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

words.meaning: may we two bear ill will

closing.translation: Om. May He protect us both together. May He nourish us both together. May we work together with vigour. May what we study be full of light. May we never bear ill will towards each other. Om. Peace, peace, peace.
notes: The peace invocation of teacher and student, recited before and after the study of this Upaniṣad. It is not part of the DCS text; the wording is that of the edition of Śaṅkara's bhāṣya, which prints it at the opening and again after the last verse.
Śaṅkara's Kaṭha bhāṣya does not comment on this mantra.

sanskrit.deva:
ऊर्ध्वमूलो अवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिंल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ūrdhvamūlo avākśākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ |
tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate |
tasmiṃllokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana |
etad vai tat || 1 ||

lines.iast: ūrdhvamūlo avākśākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ
tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate
tasmiṃllokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana
lines.deva: तस्मिंल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन

lines.iast: etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: ūrdhva-mūlaḥ avāk-śākhaḥ eṣaḥ aśvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ tat eva śukram tat brahma tat eva amṛtam ucyate tasmin lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tat u na atyeti kaścana etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: ऊर्ध्व-मूलः अवाक्-शाखः एषः अश्वत्थः सनातनः तत् एव शुक्रम् तत् ब्रह्म तत् एव अमृतम् उच्यते तस्मिन् लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तत् उ न अत्येति कश्चन एतत् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: “This is the ancient fig tree, with its root above and its branches below. That root alone is the pure, that is Brahman, that alone is called the immortal. In it all the worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the vallī: as the root of a tree is ascertained by ascertaining its cotton (tūla), so this vallī ascertains the tree of saṃsāra, the effect, in order to determine the nature of its root, Brahman.

Śaṅkara: the tree is the tree of worldly existence, reaching from the unmanifest down to unmoving things. Its root, above, is the highest state of Viṣṇu. It is called a tree (vṛkṣa) because it can be cut down, and aśvattha because, like that tree, it is always trembling, shaken by the wind of desire and action. Its branches are heaven, hell, and the states of animals and departed spirits. It is ‘ancient’ because it has no beginning. It is felled by the weapon of non-attachment that comes from seeing Brahman as the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
यदिदं किंच जगत्सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् ।
महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yad idaṃ kiṃca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam |
mahad bhayaṃ vajram udyataṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti || 2 ||

lines.iast: yad idaṃ kiṃca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam
lines.deva: यदिदं किंच जगत्सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम्

lines.iast: mahad bhayaṃ vajram udyataṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti

padaccheda.iast: yat idam kiṃca jagat sarvam prāṇe ejati niḥsṛtam mahat bhayam vajram udyatam ye etat viduḥ amṛtāḥ te bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: यत् इदम् किंच जगत् सर्वम् प्राणे एजति निःसृतम् महत् भयम् वज्रम् उद्यतम् ये एतत् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: “This whole world, whatever there is, has come forth from Brahman, the life-breath, and moves in it. It is a great terror, a thunderbolt raised. Those who know this become immortal.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this answers the view that the world arose from nothing. prāṇa is the supreme Brahman. As servants keep to their master's command on seeing him before them with thunderbolt raised, so this world of sun, moon, planets and stars keeps to its order without a moment's rest.

sanskrit.deva:
भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः ।
भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhayād asyāgnis tapati bhayāt tapati sūryaḥ |
bhayād indraś ca vāyuś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ || 3 ||

lines.iast: bhayād asyāgnis tapati bhayāt tapati sūryaḥ
bhayād indraś ca vāyuś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ

padaccheda.iast: bhayāt asya agniḥ tapati bhayāt tapati sūryaḥ bhayāt indraḥ ca vāyuḥ ca mṛtyuḥ dhāvati pañcamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: भयात् अस्य अग्निः तपति भयात् तपति सूर्यः भयात् इन्द्रः च वायुः च मृत्युः धावति पञ्चमः

translations.text: “From fear of him fire burns; from fear of him the sun gives heat; from fear of him Indra, the wind, and Death, the fifth, run to their tasks.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘him’ is the supreme Lord. Were there no ruler over these mighty guardians of the world, their regular activity, like that of servants in fear of their master, could not be explained.

sanskrit.deva:
इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्शरीरस्य विस्रसः ।
ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
iha ced aśakad boddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ |
tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate || 4 ||

lines.iast: iha ced aśakad boddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ
tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate

padaccheda.iast: iha cet aśakat boddhum prāk śarīrasya visrasaḥ tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīra-tvāya kalpate
padaccheda.deva: इह चेत् अशकत् बोद्धुम् प्राक् शरीरस्य विस्रसः ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीर-त्वाय कल्पते

translations.text: “If one has been able to know it here, before the body falls away, one is freed; if not, one becomes fit to take a body in the worlds of creation.”

notes: Śaṅkara supplies what is left unsaid: one who knows Brahman, the cause of that fear, while still living is released from the bondage of worldly existence; one who has not is embodied again. So the effort to know the Self must be made before the body falls, for only here is the Self seen clearly, like a face in a mirror.

sanskrit.deva:
यथादर्शे तथात्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके ।
यथाप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathādarśe tathātmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke |
yathāpsu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayor iva brahmaloke || 5 ||

lines.iast: yathādarśe tathātmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke
lines.deva: यथादर्शे तथात्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके

lines.iast: yathāpsu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayor iva brahmaloke
lines.deva: यथाप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके

padaccheda.iast: yathā ādarśe tathā ātmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛ-loke yathā apsu pari iva dadṛśe tathā gandharva-loke chāyā-ātapayoḥ iva brahma-loke
padaccheda.deva: यथा आदर्शे तथा आत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृ-लोके यथा अप्सु परि इव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्व-लोके छाया-आतपयोः इव ब्रह्म-लोके

words.meaning: in the world of the ancestors
in the world of the gandharvas

translations.text: “As in a mirror, so it is seen in oneself; as in a dream, so in the world of the ancestors; as it is seen, so to speak, in water, so in the world of the gandharvas; as shade and light, so in the world of Brahmā.”

notes: pari … dadṛśe is one verb (paridadṛśe), its parts separated in the verse.

Śaṅkara: in one's own intellect, when it is clear as a mirror, the Self is seen quite distinctly. In the world of the ancestors the sight is blurred, as in a dream, and likewise in the world of the gandharvas, as a reflection in water. Only in the world of Brahmā is it as distinct as shade from light, and that world is hard to reach. Therefore the effort must be made here.

sanskrit.deva:
इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् ।
पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvam udayāstamayau ca yat |
pṛthag utpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati || 6 ||

lines.iast: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvam udayāstamayau ca yat
pṛthag utpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati

padaccheda.iast: indriyāṇām pṛthagbhāvam udaya-astamayau ca yat pṛthak utpadyamānānām matvā dhīraḥ na śocati
padaccheda.deva: इन्द्रियाणाम् पृथग्भावम् उदय-अस्तमयौ च यत् पृथक् उत्पद्यमानानाम् मत्वा धीरः न शोचति

translations.text: “Knowing that the senses, which arise separately, are different in nature, and that the rising and setting are theirs, the wise man does not grieve.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the senses arise separately from their causes, space and the rest, each to grasp its own object, and are wholly unlike the Self, which is pure consciousness alone. Their rising and setting, in waking and sleep, do not belong to the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvam uttamam |
sattvād adhi mahānātmā mahato 'vyaktam uttamam || 7 ||

lines.iast: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvam uttamam
sattvād adhi mahānātmā mahato 'vyaktam uttamam

padaccheda.iast: indriyebhyaḥ param manaḥ manasaḥ sattvam uttamam sattvāt adhi mahān ātmā mahataḥ avyaktam uttamam
padaccheda.deva: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परम् मनः मनसः सत्त्वम् उत्तमम् सत्त्वात् अधि महान् आत्मा महतः अव्यक्तम् उत्तमम्

translations.text: “Higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; above the intellect is the great self; higher than the great is the unmanifest.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the Self is not to be sought outside, for it is the inmost of all; this is how. The objects are here included with the senses, being of the same kind. sattva means the intellect. The rest is as at 1.3.10–11.

sanskrit.deva:
अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च ।
यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako 'liṅga eva ca |
yaṃ jñātvā mucyate jantur amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati || 8 ||

lines.iast: avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako 'liṅga eva ca
lines.deva: अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च

lines.iast: yaṃ jñātvā mucyate jantur amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati
lines.deva: यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति

padaccheda.iast: avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣaḥ vyāpakaḥ aliṅgaḥ eva ca yam jñātvā mucyate jantuḥ amṛta-tvam ca gacchati
padaccheda.deva: अव्यक्तात् तु परः पुरुषः व्यापकः अलिङ्गः एव च यम् ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुः अमृत-त्वम् च गच्छति

translations.text: “But higher than the unmanifest is the Person, all-pervading and without any mark. Knowing him, a creature is freed and attains immortality.”

notes: Śaṅkara: a mark (liṅga) is that by which a thing is inferred, such as the intellect; he has none, being free of every property of worldly existence. Knowing him from teacher and scripture, one is freed while still living from the knots of the heart, such as ignorance, and attains immortality when the body falls.

sanskrit.deva:
न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् ।
हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिकॢप्तो य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam |
hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti || 9 ||

lines.iast: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam
lines.deva: न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम्

lines.iast: hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
lines.deva: हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिकॢप्तो य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति

padaccheda.iast: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścana enam hṛdā manīṣā manasā abhikḷptaḥ ye etat viduḥ amṛtāḥ te bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपम् अस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चन एनम् हृदा मनीषा मनसा अभिकॢप्तः ये एतत् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति

words.meaning: by the ruler of the mind

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “His form does not stand within sight; no one sees him with the eye. He is revealed by the intellect that dwells in the heart and rules the mind, through reflection. Those who know this become immortal.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the eye stands for all the senses. hṛdā: by the intellect seated in the heart. manīṣā is taken as the instrumental of manīṣ, ‘that which rules (īṣṭe) the mind’, again the intellect, free of wavering. manasā: by right seeing in the form of reflection. abhikḷpta: made clear; ‘the Self can be known’ is to be supplied.
The DCS data has a damaged character where ḷ should stand in abhikḷpto; it is corrected here.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह ।
बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टति तामाहुः परमां गतिम् ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha |
buddhiś ca na viceṣṭati tām āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim || 10 ||

lines.iast: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha
buddhiś ca na viceṣṭati tām āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim
lines.deva: बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टति तामाहुः परमां गतिम्

padaccheda.iast: yadā pañca avatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha buddhiḥ ca na viceṣṭati tām āhuḥ paramām gatim
padaccheda.deva: यदा पञ्च अवतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह बुद्धिः च न विचेष्टति ताम् आहुः परमाम् गतिम्

translations.text: “When the five senses of knowledge, together with the mind, stand still, and the intellect does not stir, that, they say, is the highest state.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this teaches the yoga by which that intellect is gained. The senses are called ‘knowledges’ because they serve knowledge; they are withdrawn from their objects and rest in the Self, together with the mind turned back from intention and the like.

sanskrit.deva:
तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् ।
अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tāṃ yogam iti manyante sthirām indriyadhāraṇām |
apramattas tadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau || 11 ||

lines.iast: tāṃ yogam iti manyante sthirām indriyadhāraṇām
apramattas tadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau

padaccheda.iast: tām yogam iti manyante sthirām indriya-dhāraṇām apramattaḥ tadā bhavati yogaḥ hi prabhava-apyayau
padaccheda.deva: ताम् योगम् इति मन्यन्ते स्थिराम् इन्द्रिय-धारणाम् अप्रमत्तः तदा भवति योगः हि प्रभव-अप्ययौ

translations.text: “That steady holding of the senses they regard as yoga. One must then be vigilant, for yoga comes and goes.”

notes: Śaṅkara: though called yoga, ‘union’, this state is really disunion, a separation from contact with every evil; in it the Self stands in its own nature, free of what ignorance lays upon it. Vigilance is enjoined from the time one begins yoga, for yoga is subject to arising and passing away.

sanskrit.deva:
नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा ।
अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā |
astīti bruvato 'nyatra kathaṃ tad upalabhyate || 12 ||

lines.iast: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā
lines.deva: नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा

lines.iast: astīti bruvato 'nyatra kathaṃ tad upalabhyate

padaccheda.iast: na eva vācā na manasā prāptum śakyaḥ na cakṣuṣā asti iti bruvataḥ anyatra katham tat upalabhyate
padaccheda.deva: न एव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुम् शक्यः न चक्षुषा अस्ति इति ब्रुवतः अन्यत्र कथम् तत् उपलभ्यते

translations.text: “It cannot be reached by speech, nor by the mind, nor by the eye. How can it be perceived by anyone other than one who says ‘it is’?”

notes: Śaṅkara: this meets the objection that what no organ grasps does not exist. Though free of every distinction, the Self certainly exists, being known as the root of the world: an effect traced back ends in being, as a pot is always found joined to clay. One who says ‘it is’ is the believer who follows scripture; the denier, for whom the world ends in nothing, cannot perceive Brahman at all.

sanskrit.iast:
astīty evopalabdhavyas tattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ |
astīty evopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati || 13 ||

lines.iast: astīty evopalabdhavyas tattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ
astīty evopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati

padaccheda.iast: asti iti eva upalabdhavyaḥ tattva-bhāvena ca ubhayoḥ asti iti eva upalabdhasya tattva-bhāvaḥ prasīdati
padaccheda.deva: अस्ति इति एव उपलब्धव्यः तत्त्व-भावेन च उभयोः अस्ति इति एव उपलब्धस्य तत्त्व-भावः प्रसीदति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. gen. sg.

words.meaning: to one who has perceived it

translations.text: “It is to be perceived first as ‘it is’, and then in its true nature. Of these two, when it has been perceived as ‘it is’, its true nature becomes clear.”

notes: Śaṅkara: first the Self is to be perceived as existing, through its adjuncts, the intellect and other effects that are real. Its true nature is the Self without adjuncts, beyond the ideas of being and non-being, described as ‘not this, not this’. ubhayoḥ is a genitive of selection, ‘of these two’. The true nature turns towards one who has first perceived the Self as existing.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ |
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnute || 14 ||

lines.iast: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ
lines.deva: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः

lines.iast: atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnute

padaccheda.iast: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmāḥ ye asya hṛdi śritāḥ atha martyaḥ amṛtaḥ bhavati atra brahma samaśnute
padaccheda.deva: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामाः ये अस्य हृदि श्रिताः अथ मर्त्यः अमृतः भवति अत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: “When all the desires lodged in his heart fall away, then the mortal becomes immortal; here he attains Brahman.”

notes: Śaṅkara: for one who sees the true Self there is nothing else left to desire. The heart is the intellect, which, and not the Self, is the seat of desires. With death in the form of ignorance, desire and action destroyed, there is no going anywhere: here itself, like a lamp gone out, every bond is stilled and he becomes Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ |
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty etāvaddhyanuśāsanam || 15 ||

lines.iast: yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty etāvaddhyanuśāsanam

padaccheda.iast: yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasya iha granthayaḥ atha martyaḥ amṛtaḥ bhavati etāvat hi anuśāsanam
padaccheda.deva: यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्य इह ग्रन्थयः अथ मर्त्यः अमृतः भवति एतावत् हि अनुशासनम्

translations.text: “When all the knots of the heart are cut through here, then the mortal becomes immortal. This much alone is the teaching.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the knots are the notions born of ignorance that bind fast, such as ‘I am this body’, ‘this wealth is mine’, ‘I am happy, I am unhappy’. They are destroyed, while one still lives, by the opposite knowledge, ‘I am Brahman and am not bound to birth and death’; the desires that spring from them then perish at the root. ‘This much’: this and no more is the teaching of all the Upaniṣads.

sanskrit.deva:
शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका ।
तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवति ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā |
tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavati || 16 ||

lines.iast: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā
lines.deva: शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका

lines.iast: tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavati

padaccheda.iast: śatam ca ekā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyaḥ tāsām mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtā ekā tayā ūrdhvam āyan amṛta-tvam eti viṣvaṅ anyāḥ utkramaṇe bhavati
padaccheda.deva: शतम् च एका च हृदयस्य नाड्यः तासाम् मूर्धानम् अभिनिःसृता एका तया ऊर्ध्वम् आयन् अमृत-त्वम् एति विष्वङ् अन्याः उत्क्रमणे भवति

words.meaning: to the crown of the head

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. sg.

translations.text: “There are a hundred and one channels of the heart. One of them goes out to the crown of the head; going upward by it, one reaches immortality. The others, leading in every direction, serve for departing.”

notes: Śaṅkara: for the knower who has become Brahman in this life there is no going at all. This verse is about those who know Brahman less perfectly, or follow other meditations, and go to the world of Brahmā; and it tells the fruit of the fire-teaching asked for earlier. The one channel is the suṣumnā. The immortality reached by it is relative, lasting to the dissolution of the elements, or it is the final immortality gained in time together with Brahmā. The other channels lead back to birth and death.
The text reads bhavati, a singular; Śaṅkara glosses it with the plural bhavanti, which the sense requires with anyāḥ.

sanskrit.deva:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः ।
तं स्वाच्छरीरात्प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण ।
तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ |
taṃ svāccharīrāt pravṛhen muñjād iveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa |
taṃ vidyācchukram amṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukram amṛtam iti || 17 ||

lines.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ
lines.deva: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः

lines.iast: taṃ svāccharīrāt pravṛhen muñjād iveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa
taṃ vidyācchukram amṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukram amṛtam iti

padaccheda.iast: aṅguṣṭha-mātraḥ puruṣaḥ antarātmā sadā janānām hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ tam svāt śarīrāt pravṛhet muñjāt iva iṣīkām dhairyeṇa tam vidyāt śukram amṛtam tam vidyāt śukram amṛtam iti
padaccheda.deva: अङ्गुष्ठ-मात्रः पुरुषः अन्तरात्मा सदा जनानाम् हृदये संनिविष्टः तम् स्वात् शरीरात् प्रवृहेत् मुञ्जात् इव इषीकाम् धैर्येण तम् विद्यात् शुक्रम् अमृतम् तम् विद्यात् शुक्रम् अमृतम् इति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “The Person, the size of a thumb, the inner Self, is always seated in the hearts of people. One should draw him out from one's own body with steadiness, like the inner stalk from muñja grass. One should know him as the pure, the immortal; one should know him as the pure, the immortal.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this sums up the meaning of all the vallīs. To ‘draw out’ is to set the Self apart from the body, as pure consciousness alone. The repetition, and the word iti, mark the end of the Upaniṣad.

sanskrit.deva:
मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् ।
ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्युरन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo 'tha labdhvā vidyām etāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam |
brahmaprāpto virajo 'bhūd vimṛtyur anyo 'py evaṃ yo vid adhyātmam eva || 18 ||

lines.iast: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo 'tha labdhvā vidyām etāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam
lines.deva: मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम्

lines.iast: brahmaprāpto virajo 'bhūd vimṛtyur anyo 'py evaṃ yo vid adhyātmam eva

padaccheda.iast: mṛtyu-proktām naciketaḥ atha labdhvā vidyām etām yoga-vidhim ca kṛtsnam brahma-prāptaḥ virajaḥ abhūt vimṛtyuḥ anyaḥ api evam yaḥ vit adhyātmam eva
padaccheda.deva: मृत्यु-प्रोक्ताम् नचिकेतः अथ लब्ध्वा विद्याम् एताम् योग-विधिम् च कृत्स्नम् ब्रह्म-प्राप्तः विरजः अभूत् विमृत्युः अन्यः अपि एवम् यः वित् अध्यात्मम् एव

translations.text: Then Naciketas, having received this knowledge taught by Death, and the whole method of yoga, attained Brahman and became free from stain and free from death. So too will anyone else who thus knows the inner Self.

notes: Śaṅkara: this closes the story, in praise of the knowledge. ‘The whole’: with its means and its fruit. viraja: free of merit and demerit; vimṛtyu: free of desire and ignorance. evaṃvit: one who knows the inner Self in the way described; ‘he too becomes free from death’ is to be supplied.
naciketaḥ here is a nominative (naciketā in some editions), the subject of abhūt.
